clue.text: Alumnus of Eton, and furthermore Cambridge University, and finally Dartmouth

parts.note: a postscript, PS, is what you add to a letter as a further remark
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, a university in Cambridge, Massachusetts

indicators.note: finally asks for only the closing letter of the word Dartmouth

explanation.surface: A list of the institutions an Old Etonian went on to attend, ending with the naval college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cambridge University' looks English but points to the other Cambridge, in Massachusetts; Dartmouth is likewise an American college as well as a naval one.
explanation.definitionFit: Wodehouse's monocled character of that name was educated at Eton, as he likes to mention.

clue.text: With archaic article, this writer could produce a soporific state

indicators.note: the wordplay works backwards: the answer with an extra word attached would make the soporific state, so that word is taken away

parts.note: shut-eye is informal for sleep
ye is the old written form of the definite article 'the'

explanation.surface: A writer whose books, given an old-fashioned 'the', might send you to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as the answer plus YE making SHUT-EYE; take YE away from SHUTEYE to leave the writer. 'could produce' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevil Shute was the English novelist who wrote A Town Like Alice and On the Beach.

clue.text: A solitary type in coral island castaway Ralph, covered by Times?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: covered by means the castaway's surname sits between the letters given by Times

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, so two of them, TT, are times
Ralph Rover narrates Ballantyne's The Coral Island, about boys shipwrecked on a Pacific island

explanation.surface: A question whether the lonely boy shipwrecked in The Coral Island was reviewed in The Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but it is the plural of the abbreviation T.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone turned inward who prefers their own company is a solitary type.

clue.text: Melville, to Elizabeth Knapp Shaw?

definitions.meaning: the first name of the author of Moby-Dick
Elizabeth Knapp Shaw married the novelist, so to her he was her husband, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Herman was Melville's given name, and read as two words it is what a wife might call her husband.

clue.text: Jackal maybe at home with a pair of donkeys

parts.note: an ass is a donkey, so a pair is two of the word
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: Someone at home looking after a couple of donkeys.
explanation.walkthrough: The Jackal is the hired killer in Frederick Forsyth's The Day of the Jackal; 'maybe' marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jackal is a professional killer hired to murder de Gaulle, so he is an example of a hitman.

clue.text: A storm's brewing after report of illicit liaison: source is a wartime story

indicators.note: after places the brewed letters later in the answer than the spoken piece
report of means the word for the liaison is to be heard spoken, giving letters that sound the same

parts.note: an affair is an illicit romantic relationship
a well is a source of water

indicators.note: a storm that is brewing is still forming, so its letters are not yet in shape

parts.note: the possessive 's is no letter, leaving the word storm

explanation.surface: A war novel's origin in a sordid affair, with trouble brewing.
explanation.walkthrough: AFFAIR said aloud gives A FARE; 'brewing' turns A STORM into TO ARMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemingway's novel of the Italian front in the First World War is a story set in wartime.

clue.text: On the left side of Mackenzie's street

definitions.meaning: in heraldry and in Latin the word means on the left-hand side
... Street is a 1913 novel by Compton Mackenzie

explanation.definitionFit: The heraldic term for the left-hand side also names the street in the title of Compton Mackenzie's best-known novel.

clue.text: Shabby in appearance, a la Pip?

definitions.meaning: a pip is a fruit's seed, so like a pip means full of seeds; Pip is also the hero of Great Expectations

explanation.definitionFit: Seedy means down-at-heel, and literally means full of pips.

clue.text: Christopher Robin's home after one

indicators.note: after places the outlaw's forest behind the numeral

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
Sherwood Forest is the legendary home of Robin Hood

explanation.surface: Christopher Robin, of the Winnie-the-Pooh books, going home after one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christopher Robin' looks like one name, but the definition stops at 'Christopher' and Robin is Robin Hood.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood was the English novelist of Goodbye to Berlin, so he is identified by his first name.

clue.text: He could be brandishing antique arm

indicators.note: brandishing means waving about, so these letters are swung into a new order

explanation.surface: A man who may be waving an old weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Allan Quatermain, H. Rider Haggard's big-game hunter, is a male character, so 'He' stands for him.

clue.text: Allusion penned by Kate Chopin

indicators.note: penned by means held inside the writer's name, as if written by her and enclosed there

explanation.surface: A literary reference written by the American author of The Awakening.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint reminder of an earlier work, as in 'echoes of Flaubert', is an allusion to it.

clue.text: Before start of exam, do least revision of The Waste Land?

indicators.note: Before puts the rearranged letters ahead of the exam's first letter
revision means the letters are worked over into a new order, as in revising notes
start of means only the first letter of the word exam

explanation.surface: A student told to do as little revision as possible of Eliot's poem before the exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision' looks like exam study, but it is the anagram signal: DO LEAST becomes DESOLAT, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliot's poem portrays a barren, ruined landscape, and 'desolate' describes such bleak emptiness.

clue.text: Detective writer's regular forays into scary genres

indicators.note: regular forays means dipping into the words at even intervals, taking every other letter

explanation.surface: A crime novelist who regularly ventures into horror.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothy L. Sayers wrote the Lord Peter Wimsey detective novels.

clue.text: "Poems are made by fools like me, / But only God can make a —" (Joyce Kilmer)

definitions.text: "Poems are made by fools like me, / But only God can make a —" (Joyce Kilmer)

parts.words: "Poems are made by fools like me, / But only God can make a —" (Joyce Kilmer)
parts.note: the closing couplet of Kilmer's best-known poem, with its last word left blank for the solver to supply

explanation.definitionFit: Kilmer's 1913 poem ends with these lines, naming the leafy plant only God can make.

clue.text: King Lear: he's a deviant in practice

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

indicators.note: deviant means straying from the norm, so the letters stray from their order

parts.note: taken as its letters, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's King Lear described as a wayward figure in his habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Lear' looks like the play title, but King gives just R.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice run of a play before it is performed.

clue.text: One's inspired by poet coming out

indicators.note: inspired literally means breathed in, so the numeral is drawn into the poet's name

parts.note: Ralph Waldo Emerson was an American poet and essayist
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone drawing inspiration from a poet as they make their debut.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergence from water or from hiding is a coming out.

clue.text: Brainless character's panic meeting one involved in murder

parts.note: a scare is a sudden panic
a murder is the collective noun for crows

explanation.surface: A dim-witted figure panics on meeting someone mixed up in a killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'murder' suggests a crime, but it is the word for a flock of crows.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Wizard of Oz the straw man wants a brain, so he is the brainless character.

clue.text: Amid plot twists one's seen in The Ambassadors?

indicators.note: plot twists suggest a story turning, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone appearing amid the twists of Henry James's novel The Ambassadors.
explanation.definitionFit: Envoys sent abroad, such as ambassadors, are members of the diplomatic service.

clue.text: German work on the stage losing leading pair of actors separately

indicators.note: losing means some letters drop out of the word for 'on the stage'
separately says the two lost letters are not side by side

parts.note: theatrical means of or on the stage
the opening two letters of the word actors

explanation.surface: A German play on the stage loses its two lead actors.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the A and the C, apart from each other, from THEATRICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trial is Kafka's novel, originally written in German as Der Process.

clue.text: Assistant editor retired after introduction of ChatGPT?

indicators.note: after places the turned editor behind the AI

parts.note: ChatGPT's introduction brought artificial intelligence, AI, to the public

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, so the editor's letters go backwards

explanation.surface: An editorial assistant forced to retire once ChatGPT arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduction' does not take a first letter here; it stands for what ChatGPT brought in, AI.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is a helper or assistant to someone senior.

clue.text: Finally, absurdist playwright's back as children's author

indicators.note: back means the letters gathered so far are read in reverse
Finally takes only the closing letter of absurdist

parts.note: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: An absurdist dramatist finally returns as a writer for children.
explanation.walkthrough: T (end of absurdist) plus IBSEN makes TIBSEN, which 'back' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Nesbit wrote The Railway Children and other classic children's books.

clue.text: Thirteen who collaborated with Hardy

definitions.meaning: points to the answer at 13-across, of which the bay is an example
Stan ... was Oliver Hardy's comedy partner

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' suggests Thomas Hardy, but it is Oliver Hardy of the comedy double act.
explanation.definitionFit: The bay is an evergreen, so it fits the 13-across answer, and Stan of that name partnered Oliver Hardy.

clue.text: Literature's unromantic style is disappearing field of study

indicators.note: disappearing means the word before it vanishes from the style's name

parts.note: realism is the literary mode that depicts life plainly, without romantic idealising

explanation.surface: The unromantic realist style of fiction is fading as an academic subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a domain or sphere, as in 'the realm of physics'.

clue.text: Get a poster remade after cancellation of G&S … ?

definitions.text: Get a poster remade after cancellation of G&S … ?

indicators.note: remade means the letters are rebuilt in a different order
after cancellation of means two letters are first struck out from the shuffled pool

parts.note: the initials of Gilbert and Sullivan

explanation.surface: Advice to reprint a playbill once a Gilbert and Sullivan show is called off.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle GET A POSTER less its G and S; the result is the kind of piece G&S wrote, hence the whole clue defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's comic works such as The Mikado are light operas.

clue.text: Jarndyce's friend, no boy, is an ancient character

indicators.note: no means without, so the boy is taken away from the friend's name

parts.note: Lawrence Boythorn is John Jarndyce's old friend in Dickens's Bleak House

explanation.surface: A friend in Bleak House, no longer a boy, is an old character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' suggests a person in the novel; here it is a letter of an old alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: This runic letter, used in Old English for the th sound, is an ancient written character.

clue.text: Second half of Disney film The Jungle Book's setting (broadly speaking)

indicators.note: Second half of keeps only the latter four of the film title's eight letters

parts.note: Fantasia is Disney's 1940 animated film set to classical music

explanation.surface: The latter part of a Disney film set where The Jungle Book takes place.
explanation.walkthrough: The Jungle Book is set in India, so the continent is its setting only 'broadly speaking'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's stories take place in the Indian jungle, which lies within that continent.

clue.text: Mancunian mayor Burnham's opening rant broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are thrown into a new order
opening means just the first letter of Burnham

explanation.surface: Andy Burnham, Manchester's mayor, has his opening rant aired on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mancunian' looks like an adjective for the mayor, but it defines Gaskell's novel set in Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Gaskell's novel follows a working-class heroine from Manchester, making her a Mancunian.

clue.text: Introduction to Canterbury Tales I'm developing that might be called "Traveller's Joy"?

indicators.note: Introduction to takes only the opening letter of Canterbury
developing means evolving into another form, so the letters change their order

parts.note: taken as its letters, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Chaucer's Canterbury Tales described as a delight for those on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traveller's Joy' sounds like a description of pilgrims' tales, but it is the folk name of a wild climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Traveller's joy is the country name of the wild climbing plant Clematis vitalba.

clue.text: What's essential for illustrator? Outstanding drawing

indicators.note: the essential part of a word is its central core, so take the middle letter of illustrator

parts.note: an outstanding debt is one still owing

explanation.surface: Asking what an illustrator needs most, and answering: excellent draughtsmanship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' looks like sketching but means pulling, as a truck pulls a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Hauling a vehicle behind you is drawing it along.
